title: fix(plugin-security)!: a delegated operation runs only in an organization the delegator's membership backs
body:
Fixes #25063

Clause-②: no (narrowing) — on a walled posture, an operation of an on-behalf-of context whose active organization the delegator's membership does not back is refused `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`, where it used to run.

Seat call of record: `6312131621` on the card (option P, narrowing confirmed). The claim `6311248489` was widened in place to the prologue and the three pins' files. ⛔ Disclosure (#9387 ruling `5323310017`): this body states the rule and an abstract reach only.

## The rule

ADR-0090 D10 bounds a delegated operation by the delegator's scope. The operation runs in the live principal's active organization, and `resolveDelegatorContext` resolves the delegator in that same organization, assuming the agent and its delegator are in the same organization. Nothing checked that assumption.

The delegated-principal prologue (`resolveOperationPrincipals`, `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts`) now checks it. It sits beside the dangling-delegator refusal and runs before any gate. It refuses `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`, for every verb, when all three hold:

- the tenancy posture enforces the organization wall (`isolated` or `group`);
- the on-behalf-of context carries a live active organization;
- `vetOrganizationClaim(liveOrganization, delegator.accessible_org_ids, posture)` answers `undefined`. This is the one existing spelling of "a membership backs this organization", called rather than copied.

No error code is added. The message names the organization and the delegator, and the developer message carries the `[ADR-0090 D10]` tag. This PR implements ADR-0090 D10 and does not edit the ADR.

## Reach, abstractly

Reach was shown in process under both walled postures. No public door builds the refused shape: the `/mcp` OAuth door, the one producer of an on-behalf-of context, vets the request's organization against the same membership. Runtime's `resolve-execution-context.oauth-organization.test.ts`, which drives that producer into the real `SecurityPlugin`, stays green against the rebuilt `dist/`.

## Boundary, before and after

- **Before:** under `isolated` or `group`, an on-behalf-of operation in an organization the delegator is not a member of ran, answered by the gates the middleware composed for the two principals.
- **After:** that operation is refused `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` at the prologue, every verb, and nothing runs.
- **Unchanged:**
  - the `single` posture, because `vetOrganizationClaim` answers the claim unchanged there;
  - an on-behalf-of context with no active organization, which keeps ADR-0123 D2's answers;
  - a context without `onBehalfOf`;
  - a dangling delegator, still refused as before;
  - system contexts, which never reach the prologue;
  - every context the `/mcp` door builds.

## Pins

- **New: `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/delegated-organization-membership.test.ts`** (25 cases). It runs on real `ObjectQL` (source), a real `SqlDriver` and a real `SecurityPlugin`, with the delegator rebuilt from stored `sys_user` / `sys_member` / `sys_user_permission_set` rows.
  - **Refusal cells (16):** `group` and `isolated` × a public and a private object × a single insert, an array insert, a read, and an update plus a delete. Each asserts `code: 'PERMISSION_DENIED'`, status `403`, the `[ADR-0090 D10]` developer-message tag and the two subjects the message names. Each also asserts nothing stored or changed. The delegator holds the private object's grant in every organization involved, so the D10 grant intersection never answers for it.
  - **Preservation cells (9):** per walled posture, a delegated insert and read in an organization the delegator belongs to; the same caller without the delegation link; a delegated context with no active organization (ADR-0123 D2's refusal, by its tag); and a system context. Plus the `single` posture.
  - The file passes a no-op `hook`, so `kernel:ready` never fires, as other real-stack files here do. Without it, the plugin starts its platform bootstrap un-awaited, and a short case destroys the engine under that bootstrap's reads (knex `Acquire connection error: aborted` noise; no case failed).
- **Rewritten, because each built a delegated context in an organization the delegator does not belong to:**
  1. `tenant-layer0-verdict-on-operation.test.ts`, "the recorded verdict is the INTERSECTION — an organization set neither wall names alone". The delegator's memberships go from `org-2, org-3, org-9` to `org-1, org-3, org-9`, so they include the live `org-1`. The asserted walls and the recorded intersection move with them, from `org-2, org-3` to `org-1, org-3`. That is still a set neither wall names alone. Its control case ("the SAME fixture without the delegation link") takes the same memberships so it stays the same fixture.
  2. Same file, "a delegator with NO membership makes the recorded verdict `deny`". A delegator with no membership backs no organization, so this case cannot move to an in-set organization. The caller now carries no active organization instead: the prologue has nothing to vet, and the composed wall's `deny` is still the subject.
  3. `objects/default-row-scope-declarations.test.ts`, persona "mcp agent for the platform admin". The fixture gains a `sys_member` row for `p_admin` in `org_x`, the organization every agent persona's request runs in. The expected rows are unchanged.
- No other fixture went red. The full `plugin-security` suite is listed below. The one dependent test that drives an on-behalf-of context into the real `SecurityPlugin` is runtime's OAuth-organization file, and it is green.

## Ablation

- **Method:** the check was disabled (`false &&` on its first conjunct) through `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, in WRAP mode with its own restore. The subject is imported from source, so there is no `dist/` leg.
- **Predicted before the run:** the 16 refusal cells go red, and the 9 preservation cells and both rewritten files stay green.
- **Observed:** `Tests 16 failed | 63 passed (79)`, and the 16 are exactly the refusal cells. Each became an admitted operation, except where the walls composed for the two principals already hid the row (`RECORD_NOT_FOUND` on a `group` update).
- **Restore:** the blob after restore equals HEAD (`2f6dfd3fd761`), and `git diff HEAD` is empty.

## Tests and gates (head `3da7379b5`)

- `plugin-security` full suite: `Test Files 205 passed (205) · Tests 4202 passed | 45 skipped (4247)`, `VERDICT command-exit 0`.
- `plugin-security` `typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit`, the scripts project, and `check:test-typecheck`): exit 0, with 0 files / 0 errors / 0 pinned signatures in the test-typecheck debt ledger.
- runtime: `resolve-execution-context.oauth-organization.test.ts` and `http-dispatcher.test.ts`, against `plugin-security`'s rebuilt `dist/` (the rule's text was confirmed in `dist/index.mjs`): `Test Files 2 passed · Tests 264 passed`.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` (no paths) derived 69 commands from 5 paths against merge base `4feccc268`. All 69 exit 0, each exit captured before any pipe. `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `pnpm check:i18n` first exited 3 (`PREREQUISITE NOT MET`: no full build). After a full `turbo run build` both exit 0. `--ran` reads "69 derived, 69 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN" and exits 0.
- **Not run locally:** the dogfood on-behalf-of files, which build agent contexts with no active organization, so the rule is inert there by construction. They run on `main`'s battery.

## Acceptance notes

- **The rule lives at the operation prologue.** Paths that resolve a delegator on their own (explain, the admission probes, a diagnostic) do not carry the refusal. They are listed for the seat in the dev report, kept off this PR per the disclosure ruling. No door builds the shape.
- **`resolveDelegatorContext`'s comment** ("the agent and its delegator are, by construction, in the same org") could point at the prologue check. `explain-engine.ts` is outside this card's file surface, so it is left as is.
- **`origin/main` moved after the merge base** (`28c9a2cb6`, spec and driver-turso). It shares no file with this diff, so it is not merged; `dispatch-gates` reports that none of those commits touched what this derivation reads.
